## What I changed

I agreed with the finding — the `sharesHousehold → id, else none` gate was the one bit of household-id derivation duplicated across `RequireUniqueIdentity` and `AssignHousehold`, defeating the `HouseholdKey` "single definition, cannot drift apart" invariant the rest of the change leans on.

- **`HouseholdKey`** — added `candidateHouseholdId(OwnerFieldsDto)`: the one place the share-or-not gate lives, returning the deterministic id when `sharesHousehold` is true, else `null`.
- **`RequireUniqueIdentity`** — now calls `HouseholdKey.candidateHouseholdId(owner)` instead of inlining the gate; Javadoc updated (dropped the "derived exactly as `AssignHousehold` will" phrasing, since both now share one definition).
- **`AssignHousehold`** — gates on `candidateHouseholdId(request) == null` rather than re-deriving the same rule, so the assigned id and the identity-key id are computed from a single source. (It still builds a `HouseholdKey` for the `matches()` backfill — that's the matching rule, already single-defined, not the gate.)

Behaviour is unchanged: the candidate id and assigned id resolve to the same value as before (the DTO and the built `Owner` carry identical normalized `lastName`/`address`), and the acceptance test still passes.
